Two years of that plan ($79.98) costs about as much as a whole Birdfy Cam 2K ($79.99 on birdfy.com), a camera that clamps to the feeder the shopper already owns.
standout_why: I compared against these pages: Reviewed.com (cited, both URLs, 2026-11-06), Feeder Field (rank 2, uncited) and WIRED (cited; it blocked fetching, so I could not check it). Reviewed lists subscription prices product by product: Birdbuddy Family Premium $98.99/yr, Birdfy Plus $79.99/yr, Kiwibit $7.99/mo. It never adds up a total cost, and it does not cover Birdfy Cam 2 / Cam 2 4K or Wasserstein-plus-Blink. Feeder Field gives 2-year totals for all-in-one feeders only: Birdfy Feeder 2 ~$350, Feeder 2 Pro ~$400, Birdbuddy Pro Solar ~$438. It says outright that it does not cover Birdfy Cam 2 / Cam 2 4K or Wasserstein cases. So no page prices the 'camera for a feeder you own' setups, the case route ChatGPT showed included, over time.
decides: This supports leading with Birdfy Cam 2K ($79.99) or Cam 2 4K ($99.99) for a shopper who owns a feeder. The Wasserstein case ($47.99 direct, not ChatGPT's $69.99) only wins for someone who already has a Blink/Wyze/Ring camera and either already pays for that camera's plan or doesn't need clips stored in the cloud. All-in-one feeders cost $99–$199.99 up front, and their AI bird ID costs $69.99–$79.99 a year (Birdbuddy Individual Premium, Birdfy Plus). That roughly doubles over two years: Birdbuddy Home comes to $338.98 with Premium.
